safety_findings.statement: Do not close HV or charge until every cell's rest voltage is assessed: the lowest cell reached 2.420 V on closure 5 at 3606.7 s, below the 2.500 V original trip.
Five HV reclosures after protective shutdown drove cells deeper than the original trip; no restart policy was available to judge them, so this is review-level.
HV was closed 5 times after the protective shutdown at 2100.5 s (3309.0, 3379.6, 3469.4, 3541.0, 3606.7 s). Whether this was permitted cannot be judged without a restart policy.
Each of the 5 closures ended in another protective shutdown (e.g. closed 3309.0 s, tripped 3327.5 s). Do not retry closure; the pack re-trips when loaded.
The fault resets before the closures are not visible in the record (they fall in gaps). Who or what reset the fault is unknown; ask for the BMS reset log.
13 escalations (highest level 3) were observed, but there is no protection specification to judge them against; treated as the BMS acting as designed.

unknowns: Which of SOC drift, low usable capacity or current under-read caused the ~57 pp shortfall; the data cannot separate them.
Calibration history and last full charge before t=0, and the real wall-clock time between windows.
Rest voltage of every cell, and the protection thresholds and restart policy.
